text.text: The SMR-2, or Single Module ROADM 2, integrates a 4-degree WXC (Wavelength Cross Connect), pre-amplifier, booster amplifer, and optical spectrum analyzer functionality into a single slot line card. While two degrees are shown (slots 2 and 7), the 15454 M6 chassis can house up to four ROADM degrees. A 2-degree optimized version, the SMR-1, is available as well.

text.text: The 100G transponder features Cisco's 100G CP-DQPSK DWDM module, allowing for unregenerated distances of up to 3000km. By integrating a CXP client port on the same card, a 100G transponder occupies only a single slot, equating to one transponder per rack unit, or 42 per bay.

text.text: The AnyRate Xponder provides the ultimate in flexibility for sub-10G muxponding and transponding services for data, storage, video, and TDM protocols. Eight SFP ports can function in pairs as transponders, or multiplex multiple signals into protected or unprotected 10G wavelengths. Pluggable XFP ports allow a choice of cost-optimized fixed wavelength optics, or tunable high performance optics.

text.text: The 10 x 10G client card aggregates up to ten client signals for transmission across a 100G DWDM wavelength by communicating across the backplane of the 15454 M6 chassis to a 100G trunk card in an adjacent slot. Its ten SFP+ ports support 10GigE, OC-192, OTU-2, 10G Fibre Channel and 8G Fibre Channel. The 10 x 10G client card can also operate as a standalone 5 x 10G transponder, in which its ten SFP+ ports operate in pairs to form five 8G or 10G transponders.

text.text: The 100G trunk card is simply another mode of the same 100G transponder card, but communicates across the backplane of the 15454 M6 chassis, allowing sub-rate muxponding via the 10 x 10G client card, or the use of CFP client optics via the 2 x CFP client card (not shown).
